x: In 1914 a young Belgravian named Jimmy Bellchamber determined that the Club’s colours should be prominently carried over the 52 miles of road that year, but the outbreak of war caused a postponement of plans.

The meeting was opened by President Alf Harley at 6.45 p.m., who asked the assembly to stand in silence for a few moments as a mark of respect for Jimmy Bellchamber, Oscar Horwood, Joe Turner and Colin Sutton, who had passed away since our last meeting.

Harry Evans presented the new Jimmy Bellchamber Trophy (50 kilometres Walk) to the first holder Hugh McGreechan. Ted Gaworski presented a cup to Peter Porter for the best throwing performance of the year (156ft6in) with the hammer.

Despite the filthy weather, there was a good muster of club supporters and if our clothes were damped, at least our spirits were not. By his grand performance, Eric becomes this year's holder of the Jimmy Bellchamber Cup.
Jimmy Bellchamber, the Club's first great long distance walker, finished 2nd in the Brighton and Back race in 1921 in 20hrs. 53mins. 35secs. and so became our first Centurion.
